lesson.title: Diffusion, osmosis and active transport
lesson.body: Cells must take in materials such as oxygen and water and get rid of wastes. Diffusion is the movement of particles from where there are many of them (high concentration) to where there are few (low concentration). It needs no energy. Osmosis is the movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution. A plant cell that takes in water becomes firm, which is called turgid. In a very concentrated solution, a plant cell loses water and its membrane pulls away from the cell wall, which is called plasmolysis. Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient and needs energy.
lesson.audio_script: Diffusion is the movement of particles from high concentration to low concentration, and it needs no energy. Osmosis is the movement of water through a partially permeable membrane, from a dilute solution to a concentrated one. A plant cell full of water is turgid. If it loses water, it is plasmolysed. Active transport needs energy.
